metadata.value:
The Executive Recruiter will be responsible for owning and executing executive level searches. This person will need to be well-versed in the full life cycle executive search process (including candidate generation and development, senior client management and offer/negotiation.)

The role will include the following responsibilities:
Oversee the management and execution of full-life cycle executive searches by developing the sourcing and recruiting strategies across select/designated functional areas
Calibrating candidates with hiring managers
Developing those prospects into candidates, engaging them and performing initial assessment (Pitch Calls)
Participating in client update meetings on active searches and preparing reports
Conducting on-site interviews and participating in debriefs; performing reference checks and creatively negotiating complex executive compensation packages.
Support the Senior Director, Executive Recruiting on searches
Develop search strategies, conduct research, and present qualified candidates for executive searches

Required Experience and Education
6+ years of experience within Executive Recruiting
3+ years of leading VP+ level searches
1+ years of project management experience; the ability to follow-through on individual and team-wide goals, plans and projects.
1+ years experience building, and executing, strategies for staffing projects.
1+ years of experience pulling insights from data, and utilizing insights to advise hiring leaders, and influence business decisions.
 
Preferred Experience and Education
Experience in agency and in-house recruiting 
Experience recruiting at a startup and/or within the healthcare industry.
Experience building workforce forecasts
Experience partnering with staffing partners/vendors

Position Summary:
Lead technical efforts to build reliable and maintainable applications, infrastructure, and interfaces that make interacting with the health care system easier for members and providers


Primary Duties and Responsibilities
Become the expert on your team's business and technical domains
Lead the planning, execution and release of complex technical projects
Work with partners, product managers, and designers to solve challenging problems
Lead and mentor engineers on the team to improve technology and apply best practices
Independently responsible for large or complex technology capabilities (set of components or services) within their team's domain or spanning multiple domains
Facilitates, encourages, and enhances cross-team execution and collaboration; knows when cross-team projects are at risk and actively mitigates risk to deliver on time
Prolific contributor to the objectives of their functional group, as well as (potentially) organization-wide projects
Drives prioritization of technical roadmap and influences prioritization of product roadmap and process enhancements within their team
Actively identifies and reduces failure domains
Builds software to minimize effort and business impact during maintenance and failures 
Guides the development of Service-Level Objectives (SLOs) for systems they are responsible for
Own medium to large features or infrastructure projects from technical design through completion
Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations
Other duties as assigned

Required Experience and Education
6+ years of professional software engineering experience, working with a variety of technologies, and have increasingly impactful accomplishments
Experience as a major contributor cross-pod or cross-company deliverables
Experience leading technical contributions, improving the quality of what your teams create, and are excited to build fault-tolerant, and scalable software systems.
Demonstrates expertise of the practical application of CS concepts within their team.
Sets and enforces the standard for writing stable, correct, and maintainable code 
Experience mentoring and training more junior engineers

At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires.

Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 50,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.

At Linear, we are committed to quality. Security is an essential part of that quality — not a layer that we add later, but something we build in from the start. We have a foundational security program we're proud of but, as Linear evolves our product and scales into enterprise, there's meaningful work ahead: staying ahead of vulnerabilities as our attack surface grows, responding fast and cleanly when incidents happen, and hardening our product and infrastructure. As Security Engineer at Linear, you'll be operating in a high-autonomy role with real scope, doing hands-on security work across the product and infrastructure we build.

Location & work mode

Linear is a remote-first company. This role is open to candidates based in North America. You can work from anywhere within this region. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel.

What you’ll do

Depending on your experience / skillset and our broader priorities, you could:

  • Operate, automate, and extend vulnerability management end-to-end: triage, prioritize, and drive remediation across product, infrastructure, and dependencies, and keep the program’s SLAs meaningful rather than theoretical

  • Run our bug bounty program: triage incoming reports, validate severity, work with engineering on fixes, and keep researcher relationships professional and responsive

  • Lead product security testing: threat model new features (including AI/agent-facing surfaces), review designs and code for security-relevant risk, and do hands-on testing (manual and tool-assisted) rather than relying solely on scanners

  • Be a primary responder for security incidents: lead investigation and containment, drive postmortems, and turn lessons into concrete hardening work

  • Own meaningful chunks of our cloud/infra security posture on GCP/k8s/Postgres: harden configurations, close gaps surfaced by audits or scanning, and partner with infra engineering on secure defaults

  • Build and maintain security tooling and automation, including using AI/LLM tooling to speed up triage, code review, and repetitive investigation work, so the program scales without linear headcount growth

  • Partner with the GRC/Trust function: feed real findings into the risk register and control evidence, and help make sure compliance requirements reflect actual engineering practice

What we’re looking for

  • A generalist, senior-level security engineer (5+ years across security engineering, with real depth in at least two of: vulnerability management, product/appsec testing, incident response, and cloud security). We need breadth, rather than a narrow specialist in any one of these.

  • Hands-on and technical: you can read and reason about code (we use a lot of TypeScript), you’re comfortable in cloud environments (GCP a plus), and you can go deep on a finding rather than just filing a ticket for someone else to fix. You’re comfortable using AI coding/security tools as force multipliers (Linear Agent, Claude, Codex, etc).

  • Calm under pressure: you can lead an incident from first alert through postmortem without needing to be told what to do next

  • A builder: you’d rather write a script or ship a tool than repeat a manual process a third time

  • A pragmatic risk-reducer: you optimize for actually reducing risk, not for checking a box or maximizing findings count

  • Autonomy-oriented: comfortable setting your own priorities, working with significant independence, and knowing when to escalate

  • A clear communicator: able to explain a technical finding to a non-technical stakeholder and write it up so it’s actually actionable

Our tech

This is a hands-on security engineering role. You'll be running tools, reading/writing code, building detections, working in our cloud environment, and partnering closely with the engineers who build our product. Our stack is fronted by Cloudflare and runs on Google Cloud with k8s, Postgres, and Node.

For day-to-day work, we use:

  • Linear, GitHub, Slack, and Google Workspace for collaboration

  • Claude and ChatGPT for general & engineering-specific AI tasks

  • Vanta for compliance automation and evidence collection

Our security-specific tooling includes:

  • GitHub Advanced Security

  • RunReveal

  • SentinelOne

  • Health coverage (based on country requirements)

  • Paid month off after 4 years & every 2 years thereafter

  • Regular team events and off-sites

  • Remote-first with no required commute

For sales roles, this range represents on-target earnings (OTE), including base salary and variable compensation; for all other roles, it represents base salary. Wierzymy, że tworzenie oprogramowania umożliwiającego podejmowanie decyzji przez ludzi jest najlepszym sposobem na osiągnięcie tego celu. Współpracujemy z najważniejszymi instytucjami na świecie, aby przeobrazić sposób, w jaki wykorzystują dane i technologię. Nasze oprogramowanie było wykorzystywane m.in. do powstrzymania ataków terrorystycznych, odkrywania nowych leków, zdobywania przewagi na globalnych rynkach finansowych.
 
Kogo szukamy
 
Nasi klienci przychodzą do nas z przeczuciem, że jedynym sposobem na ochronę ich żołnierzy, wytwarzanie wysokiej jakości produktów, budodwanie skutecznych struktur dla opieki zdrowotnej lub zapewnianie pomocy uchodźcom jest lepsze wykorzystanie danych. Deployment Strategist jest odpowiedzialny za przekucie tego przeczucia w rzeczywistość. Praca polega przede wszystkim na odkrywaniu wskazówek i określaniu sposobu ich połączenia na podstawie dostępnych informacji.
Jeśli wierzysz w transformacyjną moc danych i technologii oraz w swoją zdolność do wykorzystania tej mocy do walki ze złożonymi problemami, chcemy poznać Cię bliżej.
 
Co robimy
 
Jako Deployment Strategist będziesz pracować w ramach zaangażowanego i kreatywnego zespołu inżynierów, projektantów produktów i innych Deployment Strategists, aby wdrażać oprogramowanie w odpowiedzi na najtrudniejsze problemy, z którymi mierzy się świat. Twoja misja polega na syntetyzowaniu oddzielnych strumieni przemyśleń w celu zrozumienia jaki problem jest najważniejszy, co mówią o nim dane, czego potrzebuje produkt, co motywuje użytkowników i na jakiej płaszczyźnie można wywrzeć największy wpływ.
Deployment Strategists to osoby, które zagłębiają się w najbardziej skomplikowane procesy i zespoły naszych klientów, oraz analizują dane i wkraczają w środowisko produktów, aby umożliwić nam odpowiednie skalowanie.. Każdy dzień jest niepowtarzalny, ale jako Deployment Strategist możesz oczekiwać, że:
 
• Spotkasz się bezpośrednio z analitykami klienta, aby zrozumieć kluczowe pytania, na które muszą odpowiedzieć, aby zlokalizować najważniejsze problemy w swoich organizacjach.
• Będziesz identyfikować istotne zbiory danych poprzez głębokie zaangażowanie w problemy i procesy klientów oraz współpracę z inżynierami pierwszej linii (Forward Deployed Engineers) w celu integracji danych w obrębie stabilnego i skalowalnego procesu.
• Będziesz współpracować z klientem, aby stworzyć dopasowane do niego sposoby pracy dla nowych grup użytkowników.
• Będziesz prowadzić sesje szkoleniowe, aby upewnić się, że produkt spełnia potrzeby użytkowników i jest wykorzystywany na skalę, mającą konkretny wpływ na działalność naszych partnerów.
• Będziesz przedstawiać wyniki naszej pracy i propozycje dotyczące przyszłej pracy odbiorcom, począwszy od analityków, a skończywszy na kadrze kierowniczej najwyższego szczebla.
• Dołączysz do naszych zespołów inżynieryjnych i projektowania produktów, aby uwzględnić obserwacje z terenu w ofercie produktów Palantira.
• Będziesz tworzyć i przedstawiać prezentacje nowym i obecnym klientom.
• Będziesz rozszerzać potencjalne zaangażowanie w nowych branżach i w coraz bardziej rozwijających się lokalizacjach na całym świecie.
 
Co sobie cenimy
 
• Członków zespołu, którzy nie są zadowoleni z powierzchownych odpowiedzi. Chęć zanurzenia się w szczegóły danych –to jest podstawa naszej pracy. A także skromność, ponieważ wyniki mają większe znaczenie niż kto zdobędzie za nie uznanie.
• Niezwykłą zdolność do rozwiązywania otwartych problemów w nieustrukturyzowanych środowiskach.
• Adaptacyjne i introspektywne podejście; chęć uczenia siebie i innych, gotowość do kierowania, jak i podążania za liderami.
• Wymagana możliwość podróżowania na poziomie 25-75%. Wymóg ten różni się w zależności od lokalizacji i zespołu.
• Plusem będzie dodatkowe doświadczenie w zakresie programowania, pisania skryptów lub używania pakietów statystycznych (np. Python, R, Matlab, SQL).
 
Wymagania:
 
• Biegła znajomość języka polskiego.
• Poświadczenie bezpieczeństwa lub możliwość do jego uzyskania.
 
 
Życie w Palantir
 
Chcemy, aby każdy z pracowników firmy Palantir osiągał najlepsze wyniki, dlatego doceniamy mocne strony, umiejętności i zainteresowania poszczególnych osób od pierwszej rozmowy kwalifikacyjnej po długoterminowy rozwój, zamiast polegać na tradycyjnych drabinach kariery. Zwracanie uwagi na potrzeby naszej społeczności umożliwia nam optymalizację naszych możliwości rozwoju i pomaga zapewnić wiele dróg do sukcesu w Palantir. Promowanie zdrowia i dobrego samopoczucia we wszystkich obszarach życia pracowników firmy Palantir to tylko jeden ze sposobów inwestowania w naszą społeczność. Dowiedz się więcej na stronie Życie w Palantir i pamiętaj, że nasza oferta może się różnić w zależności od regionu.

Wierzymy, że postępowanie zgodne z wartościami i kulturą firmy Palantir sprawia, iż pracownicy „lepiej współpracują ze sobą”, a praca osobista daje możliwość bardziej kreatywnych wyników. Dlatego zachęcamy pracowników do pracy w naszych biurach, aby wspierać powiązania i innowacje. Wiele zespołów oferuje opcje hybrydowe (dzień lub dwa dni w tygodniu pracy w domu), dzięki czemu nasi pracownicy mogą uzyskać odpowiedni kompromis dla swojej osobistej produktywności. W zależności od potrzeb biznesowych istnieje kilka ról, które pozwalają na „zdalną” pracę w wyjątkowych warunkach. Jeśli ubiegasz się o jedno z tych stanowisk, musisz pracować w mieście i kraju, w którym jesteś zatrudniony. Jeśli oferta w ogłoszeniu jest określona jako „na miejscu”, musisz pracować w biurze.

Jeśli chcesz wzmacniać najważniejsze instytucje świata, jest to miejsce dla Ciebie. Palantir ceni doskonałość niezależnie od pochodzenia. Dokładamy wszelkich starań, aby proces składania aplikacji i zatrudniania był dostępny dla wszystkich, oraz zapewnimy odpowiednie udogodnienia osobom z niepełnosprawnością. Jeśli potrzebujesz udogodnienia w procesie aplikacji lub zatrudnienia, skontaktuj się z nami i daj nam znać, jak możemy Ci pomóc.

Pamiętaj, że nigdy nie zostaniesz poproszony(-a) o przesłanie płatności lub udostępnienie informacji finansowych w celu wzięcia udziału w naszym procesie rekrutacyjnym. Jeśli podejrzewasz, że skontaktował się z Tobą oszust, zalecamy zaprzestanie wszelkiej komunikacji z taką osobą i rozważenie zgłoszenia jej odpowiednim organom, takim jak amerykańskie Centrum ds. Zgłaszania Przestępstw Internetowych (IC3) przy FBI (FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

job.descriptionPlain:
A World-Changing Company
 
At Palantir, we’re driven to solve the world's most critical and challenging problems, and believe that building software to enable human decision making is the most effective vector. We partner with the most important institutions in the world to transform how they use data and technology. Our software has been used to stop terrorist attacks, discover new medicines, gain an edge in global financial markets, and more.
 
What We're About
 
At its core, this role is about uncovering dots and—without knowing the shape they form—figuring out how to connect them. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into reality.
 
If you believe in the transformational power of data and technology and in your own ability to bring that power to bear against complex problems, we want to meet you.
 
What We Do
 
As a Deployment Strategist, you'll work as part of a driven and creative team of Engineers, Product Designers, and other Deployment Strategists to deploy software against the most challenging problems our world faces. Your mission is to synthesize disconnected streams of thought into a cohesive understanding of what the most important problem is, what the data means, what the product needs, what users are motivated by, and where the impact could be.
 
Deployment Strategists are do-ers who immerse themselves in our customers' most intricate workflows, partner with customer teams and explore the data, and dive into the product landscape to enable us to scale. A select number of Deployments Strategists may also be deployed to Palantir internal teams and problems. In this role, the problems you'll tackle will require a curious and analytical mindset, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user empathy to ultimately empower our customers to make better decisions.
 
No two days are the same, but as a Deployment Strategist you can expect to:
 
• Go onsite and meet with customer analysts to understand the critical questions they need to answer and locate their biggest pain points.
• Identify relevant datasets through deep engagement with customer problems and workflows, and work with Forward Deployed Engineers to integrate the data into a stable and extensible pipeline.
• Work with the customer to build bespoke workflows for new user groups.
• Lead training sessions to ensure that the product is meeting user needs, and to ensure it is being used widely enough to have concrete impact on our partners' operations.
• Present the results of our work and proposals for future work to audiences ranging from analysts to C-suite executives.
• Embed with our Software Engineering and Product Design teams to incorporate what you saw in the field into cross-Palantir product offerings.
• Build and deliver demos to new and existing customers.
• Scope out potential engagements in new industries and in increasingly expanding locations around the world.
 
What We Value
 
• We value team members who aren’t satisfied with surface-level answers. We value the desire to dive into the details of the data because that’s the core of our work. And we value low ego because the outcome matters more than who gets the credit.
• Extraordinary ability to take on open-ended problems in unstructured environments.
• Adaptive and introspective; willing to learn, teach, lead and follow.
• Ability to travel 25 – 75% required. Varies by location and team.
• Experience with programming, scripting or statistical packages (e.g. Python, R, Matlab, SQL) is a plus.
 
What We Require
 
• Fluency in Polish.
• Security clearance or the ability to obtain a clearance.
 
 
Life at Palantir
 

We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
 
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
 
If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process, please reach out and let us know how we can help.
 
Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

lists.content:
As an FDIE intern, your responsibilities look similar to those at a small startup, with the resources, stability, and mentorship of an established tech company. You’ll work in small teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of real infrastructure projects. Your day might span discussing systems architecture with fellow engineers, debugging a production issue, building automation to eliminate a manual process, or deploying new Palantir products across production environments.
FDIE interns are treated just like full-time engineers, with significant freedom and ownership over their work. Specifically, you can expect to:
  • Deploy and operate Palantir software across production environments, including monitoring, alerting, configuration management, and upgrades
  • Debug, improve, and optimize Palantir’s services and infrastructure with a focus on long-term reliability and scalability
  • Reduce manual operations by automating workflows, processes, and runbooks wherever possible
  • Develop novel solutions in Palantir’s Foundry and Apollo platforms to solve infrastructure challenges

• Impact: We address meaningful and exciting projects that change the world for the better.
  • Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end, working through any obstacles we may encounter. We trust each other to effectively handle time and priorities and give people the space to think for themselves.
  • Collaboration: We work with people from a variety of backgrounds — including other FDIEs, product teams, and forward deployed software engineers.
  • Growth: We believe experiential learning is one of the best teachers and encourage ourselves and our peers to seek new challenges and opportunities for growth, as well as find new ways to innovate and share knowledge.

• Ability to continuously learn, work independently, and make decisions with minimal direction
  • Confidence troubleshooting complex systems issues using observability tools and service logs
  • Comfort with large-scale production systems and technologies — such as load balancing, monitoring, distributed systems, or configuration management
  • Ability to identify and automate highly manual tasks, driving ongoing improvements within and across teams
  • Eagerness to creatively solve technical problems using cloud infrastructure, storage systems, and other infrastructure tooling
  • Ability to collaborate across teams of technical and non-technical individuals in a constantly evolving environment with dynamic objectives

• Active US Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance prior to start of internship
  • Engineering background, preferred in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, and Data Science
  • Strong proficiency with one or more programming languages, such as Python, Java, Go, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript, or similar
  • Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating

Please submit the following:
  • An updated resume / CV - please do so in PDF format
  • Thoughtful responses to our application questions

Forward Deployed Engineering is a radical commitment to the outcome. This is Palantir’s operating ethos. As an FDE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.

From hospital beds to factory floors, Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed themselves in the customer’s reality until the problem is theirs. This requires walking many miles in a customer’s shoes, building past the perimeter of what the product currently offers, and deviating from every pre-existing formula to solve the problem. Whether that problem is “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks across a power grid?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global supply chain to deliver critical parts on time?” You’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.
 
Core Responsibilities 
 
To solve mission-critical problems by deploying software and AI into the high stakes operations of the world’s leading institutions. This requires a ruthless commitment to truth-seeking and prioritizing real outcomes.

You will embed with the customer, the chaos, and the consequences, and will be entrusted with real ownership to: 
Collaborate with engineers to make architecture and design decisions
Wrestle with data at a scale that breaks assumptions and demands invention
Build custom applications, LLM workflows, and production solutions engineered for a specific customer's reality
Own relationships with stakeholders from the users in the weeds to the executives making the calls
 As an Intern, you will be entrusted with responsibility on day 1. You will not be handed a ticket queue. You will not be shielded from the customer, the chaos, or the consequences. FDEs are entrusted with real ownership, operating with real autonomy, and held to a real standard, no matter their tenure.

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
Palantir is seeking a Subcontracts Manager to join our broader U.S. Government contracts and legal team, which is key to Palantir’s mission. We’re a team that values creativity and teamwork. Whether operating solo or collaboratively, our goal is to enable our U.S. Government agency customers and partners to unlock their data and power critical operations.

In this role, you’ll provide strategic support for business-to-business relationships throughout our supply chain, including negotiating and managing subcontracts, teaming agreements, and various supplier agreements. You’ll be the primary point of contact for communications with our subcontractors and other commercial partners, and also drive communications with internal teams like business development, finance, and security compliance in order to negotiate and sign agreements with our partners. You’ll manage agreements and workflows that are critical to our U.S. Government work, including vendor and supplier contracts, programs with strategic partners, and subcontractor deliverables.

lists.content:
• Draft, review, and negotiate various contracts, including teaming agreements, subcontracts, data sharing, and license agreements
  • Support pre-award and capture efforts as well as post-award subcontract negotiation and management; including but not limited to driving the RFP process, review supplier paperwork to negotiate terms, deliverables and ensure compliance with applicable customer and regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with various internal stakeholders, including attorneys, finance, information security, and technical teams to align contractual terms with risk postures and technical requirements
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of subcontracting processes, templates, and playbooks
  • Negotiate terms of use for access to U.S. Government-furnished CUI and industry teammate portals

• Strong program / project management skills, including the ability to handle multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment, and ability to meet deadlines with minimal supervision or administrative support
  • Ability to implement legal team procedures, broader Palantir policies and procedures, and applicable regulatory and contract-specific certifications and requirements
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, with a high level of attention to detail
  • Active clearance a plus, but not required
  • Juris Doctor preferred, but not required

• 5+ years progressive experience in a Government contracts/subcontracts role
  • Eligibility to access International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR), Export Administration Regulation (EAR), Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) materials
  • Extensive experience with and knowledge of the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS)
  • Thorough knowledge of and experience with negotiating teaming agreements and prime contracts/subcontracts, and familiarity with administration for contracts ranging in size
  • Experience at a U.S. Government contractor or a tech company doing significant work with the U.S. Government
